sourceTitle: A Night at the Space Club
scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Independent English A2 asteroid comprehension assessment awaiting external pedagogical validation.

questions.q: Why is the asteroid belt not like a busy road?
choices: The asteroids stop moving there.
The rocks have a lot of empty space between them.
It is a place where only spacecraft travel.
There are no objects between Mars and Jupiter.
questions.explanation: The teacher explains that there is a lot of empty space in the asteroid belt.

questions.q: What do several observations help scientists understand?
choices: How long a school club meeting lasts.
Why the Moon is bright at night.
How to make every asteroid easier to see.
Where an asteroid is likely to travel.
questions.explanation: Paragraph two explains that observations refine our knowledge of an asteroid's orbit.

questions.q: What does Nina learn about an asteroid coming near Earth?
choices: It will always hit our planet.
Scientists cannot study its movement.
Being nearby does not automatically mean a collision.
It must be the biggest asteroid in the belt.
questions.explanation: The text clearly distinguishes coming near Earth from striking it.

questions.q: Why could Nina see Moon craters but not an asteroid?
choices: The Moon was visible, while most asteroids were too small and dark.
The teacher did not allow anyone to see asteroids.
Asteroids appear only in the early morning.
The telescope was not powerful enough to see the Moon.
questions.explanation: The class saw the Moon instead of an asteroid because asteroids were hard to see.

questions.q: What helps explain the different appearance of craters on the Moon and Earth?
choices: Scientists never study craters on our planet.
The Moon has much more water than Earth.
Weather gradually changes the surface of Earth.
Space rocks only fall on the Moon.
questions.explanation: Paragraph three says Earth has weather that slowly hides old craters.

questions.q: What was the purpose of the DART collision in the film?
choices: To test whether a small push could change an object's motion.
To collect a sample from the Moon's surface.
To prove asteroids are made only of metal.
To send astronauts to the asteroid belt.
questions.explanation: DART deliberately hit Dimorphos and changed its orbit around a larger asteroid.

questions.q: Which idea excited Nina after the short film?
choices: A school telescope could show every asteroid.
A spacecraft might change how a space rock moves.
Asteroids become stars after a collision.
The Moon has no signs of past impacts.
questions.explanation: Nina is impressed that a spacecraft can give a space rock a small push.

questions.q: A friend asks why old Moon craters are still visible. What is a good answer?
choices: The Moon has stronger winds than Earth.
The Moon's craters are painted again every year.
All Moon craters were formed last week.
There is no weather like Earth's to erase them.
questions.explanation: Paragraph three says the absence of wind and rain helps preserve Moon craters.

questions.q: Why might scientists continue to observe a newly found asteroid?
choices: To change its colour in a photograph.
To improve the calculation of its future path.
To make the object move farther away immediately.
To turn it into a small natural moon.
questions.explanation: More observations allow scientists to calculate the orbit more reliably.

questions.q: Which statement combines the two main ideas Nina learned?
choices: Asteroids are impossible to find and cannot be moved.
Any object near Earth will cause serious damage.
The best way to protect Earth is to avoid telescopes.
Watching objects and testing possible responses can help us prepare.
questions.explanation: The space club links observing asteroids with the DART experiment and future protection.
